pages.title: What Mynt is
pages.summary: Lovable for finance apps: products composed from regulated primitives, apps on top built by agents and verified by Mynt.
pages.markdown:
## The problem Mynt removes

Shipping a finance app today means a year of work before the first customer sees a screen. Which licence covers the product? Which regulator, which filings, which disclosures? Who integrates KYC, e-sign, bureau and bank data, again? And once the app exists, who proves it shows every mandated document word for word and never leaks a key?

Mynt answers all of that from one place. A licensed firm composes a product out of regulated building blocks. Mynt computes the regulation that follows. A developer asks for an app in plain words, and a verified, hosted app comes back.

## Two ideas behind everything

### 1. A financial product is a composition

Nobody designs a financial product from scratch on Mynt. You compose one from regulated building blocks called **primitives**. Each primitive is a line of business (credit, payments, insurance, …) joined to an action on it (issuance, sale, servicing, …):

- a recurring deposit is a recurring payment mandate plus a term deposit;
- a foreign-currency transfer is a currency exchange plus a payment.

Because the product is made of primitives, its regulatory regime follows from them: which regulators supervise it, which licences may provide each part, and which obligations, filings and controls apply. Mynt works all of this out from its regulatory model, so nobody has to remember it, and then checks the product's legal entity, its parties and their GRC folders against the result.

Changing a product means re-composing it, not rebuilding it. Add a part, change who provides it or tighten a term, and the new definition is checked against the regime before it goes live.

### 2. Agents build; Mynt verifies

Agents do the work on Mynt: designing, pricing, building, reviewing, prospecting. Not one of them grades its own work.

- **Every build is verified in a clean sandbox the agent never touched.** Tests, lint and types, a secrets scan, a dependency audit, an SBOM, every required disclosure, and an independent security audit all run before a pull request is opened.
- **Agents are steered by folders, not by prompts in code.** Each agent's instructions, skills and scripts live in `core/workspaces/<agent>/`, which becomes its working directory. Its skills are human-written ones found on GitHub and vendored with their licence and source.
- **Secrets never enter a sandbox or a hosted app.** Agents reach the model through Mynt's proxy with a token that dies with the run. A hosted app sends a placeholder, and the real key is added on the way out.
- **Every cost is counted.** Sandboxes, model spend and hosting are billed from metered records against per-build and monthly caps. A figure that can't be measured is never shown as $0.

## How it works, end to end

```
 idea ──► compose ──► review ──► publish ──► build ──► verify ──► host ──► customers
 innovator  primitives,  admins:    offered to    agent team    clean sandbox,  own VM,     web, mobile,
            pricing,     firm,      developers    in a sandbox, independent     gVisor,     chat
            feasibility  licences,                SDKs          audit           key at the
                         product                                  ▲             edge
                                                                  └── a failed check blocks the pull request
```

- **Primitives** are the regulated building blocks: a line of business and an action on it.
- **Products** are compositions of primitives, versioned, each with a definition, a developer contract and build terms.
- **Workspaces** (`core/workspaces/<agent>/`) steer the hosted agents: the coding team, the product desk and its algorithm explorers, the governance desk and the business-development agent.

## Who Mynt is for

Mynt's platform ships as an MCP server covering eleven lines, grouped by economic function: **credit, securitization, payments, account operations, custody and settlement, wealth, insurance, guarantees and trade, exchange, derivatives and information**.

| Who | What Mynt gives them |
| --- | --- |
| **Consumers** | Products and offers they can actually use, and a way to ask for what doesn't exist yet |
| **Builders** (innovators and developers: one role under either name) | A product foundry: composition from regulated primitives, term sheets and feasibility analysis in their own model repository, versioning, licensing checks and distribution. And apps on top of products: SDKs, APIs, webhooks, a sandbox, GTM campaigns, and coding agents that build, verify and host them. Builders needn't be licensed |
| **Licence providers** | Firms holding the licences: they sponsor builders' products under them, in the jurisdictions they cover, and can revoke a sponsorship. Their engineers connect their ledger and see pass or fail with the [partner kit](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/partners.md) |
| **Vendors** | A marketplace for standard services (identity, KYC, account data, bureau, e-sign, e-mandate) that builders plug into their products, tested by Mynt before they're listed |
| **Admins** | The regulatory model (regulators, licences, law, GRC), a governance desk that reviews firms, licences and products, and `ops_status` for what needs attention |

**Get early access:** [open an access request](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/issues/new?title=Early%20access%20request) · **Run it yourself:** [Install & build](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference.md#install--build) · **Technical reference:** [`docs/reference.md`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference.md) · **Architecture:** [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · **Partner walkthrough:** [`docs/demo.md`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/demo.md) · **Rules for coding agents:** [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/AGENTS.md)

## Ground rules

- **Secrets by name only.** Keys live in the server's environment, are never printed, and never enter a sandbox, a hosted app or a pull request.
- **Products follow their contracts.** Only the actions a product lists, where they may run; every required document shown word for word; consent before the action that needs it.
- **Agents never grade their own work.** Verification runs in a clean sandbox, and only its result decides whether a build ships.
- **No open proxy to Mynt.** On Mynt's hosting, anything an app sends to Mynt's server-side routes carries its key, so apps forward only client-session routes.
- **Dollars only for customers.** A developer's customers see and send US dollars: amounts, fees, totals, statuses, arrival times and references. Wallets, tokens, chain names, addresses and stablecoin symbols never reach an app; the USDC on Solana underneath is the licensed ramp partner's settlement rail, and Mynt refuses any service type that would show a device otherwise.
- **Nothing is guessed.** A cost that can't be measured is never shown as $0. Freestyle machine time counts the larger of Freestyle's own figure and wall-clock time.

pages.markdown:
## Front doors and their credentials

`core/src/http.ts` routes every request by path. Each door has its own authentication, and none of them accepts another's credential.

| Path | Who calls it | Authenticates with | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/mcp` | People, through any MCP client | Clerk OAuth (whitelisted users), or a local token in stdio mode | `core/src/http.ts`, `core/src/auth.ts`, `core/src/server.ts` |
| `/v1/*` (server routes) | A developer's server (`api/`) | Per-app key `mynt_live_…` / `mynt_test_…`, stored only as a SHA-256 hash | `core/src/runtime-api.ts`, `core/src/runtime.ts` |
| `/v1/client/*` | A customer's browser or phone | Client session secret `mcs_…`, at most an hour, scoped to products and actions | `core/src/runtime-api.ts` |
| `/v1/vendor/callback/<sub>` | A vendor finishing an asynchronous action | `Mynt-Signature` HMAC with the subscription's secret, 300 s window | `core/src/vendors.ts` |
| `/v1/hosting/*` | A hosted VM's agent (gateway mode) | One-time bootstrap token, then the tenant's own credentials | `core/src/hosting.ts` |
| `/agent/*` | A coding or desk agent inside its sandbox | A run token that dies with the run | `core/src/agent-proxy.ts`, `core/src/agent-meter.ts` |
| `/bd/unsubscribe` | Anyone the connector emailed | The unsubscribe link itself | `core/src/bd.ts` |
| `/healthz`, `/.well-known/*` | Load balancers, OAuth discovery | None | `core/src/http.ts` |

Locally, `mynt serve` speaks MCP over stdio for one user instead.

## How tools are registered per role

`createServer(store, user, ctx)` in `core/src/server.ts` builds a fresh MCP server **per signed-in user** and registers only the tools that user's roles allow, so a client never even sees a tool it can't call. Roles nest (`effectiveRoles` in `core/src/store.ts`):

```
admin ⊃ builder (innovator = developer) ⊃ consumer          vendor and license_provider stand beside the builder
```

Each feature module owns its tools and registers them from `server.ts`:

| Module | Tools for |
|---|---|
| `core/src/server.ts` | catalogue, consumers, enrollments, offers, apps, access requests |
| `core/src/admin.ts` | regions, product categories, the regulatory model, whitelist, oversight |
| `core/src/marketplace.ts` | entities, licences, parties, GRC folders, product composition and publishing |
| `core/src/definition-tools.ts` | v2 product definitions and developer contracts |
| `core/src/versions.ts` | product versions, diffs, restores, enrollment upgrades |
| `core/src/vendors.ts` | service types, offerings, conformance, subscriptions, firm webhooks |
| `core/src/sponsorships.ts` | licence providers' sponsorships of builders' product components |
| `core/src/runtime.ts` | API keys, webhooks, sandbox hand-offs, releases, app metrics |
| `core/src/journeys-tools.ts`, `core/src/modules.ts` | journeys, developer modules |
| `core/src/gtm.ts` | segments and campaigns |
| `core/src/build.ts`, `core/src/builds.ts` | SDKs, experiences, coding-agent builds |
| `core/src/hosting-tools.ts` | hosting, deploys, app logs and commands, VM logins |
| `core/src/desk.ts`, `core/src/explore.ts` | the product desk and algorithm explorations |
| `core/src/review.ts` | the governance desk |
| `core/src/bd.ts` | the connector (business development) |
| `core/src/take-rates.ts`, `core/src/product-requests.ts`, `core/src/ops.ts` | take rates, product requests, `ops_status` |

Every admin action, and every sensitive action by anyone, is written to `audit_log` with who did it.

pages.markdown:
## Compose, test, promote

Financial products go through the same three stages as apps (Ideas, Staging, Production), one step at a time and back down, with the same tool shapes: `get_product_promotion_checks({ product_id, to_stage })`, `promote_product({ product_id, to_stage })` and `demote_product({ product_id, to_stage, reason })`. Only the product's owner moves it (an admin, for Mynt's reference products). Every check is Mynt's own, from its records, never what an app or agent reports; each move is in the audit trail as `product_promoted` (with the checks it passed and `via`: `promote_product` or `publish_product`) or `product_demoted` (with the reason).

1. `create_product` saves a **draft**, visible only to its creator. Its stage is **idea**.
2. `test_product` runs the checks: required disclosures (description, regulator, at least 2 features), valid enums, product-line rules (credit uses `cost_of_credit` and risk `not_applicable`; insurance uses protection, guaranteed or market-linked returns), and a **misleading-claims** check that fails market-linked products promising "guaranteed", "assured" or "risk-free" returns.
3. `promote_product` to **staging** needs that test passing on what would go live, unchanged since. A product in staging is open to **sandbox builds only**: `list_buildable_products` with `environment: "sandbox"` lists it (each item carries its `stage`), `create_app` and `update_app` accept it on an app in Ideas or Staging, its builds get it (the build spec and generated SDK), and `get_product_sdk` returns its kit marked `sandbox_only`. No production app may use it: `update_app` refuses it on a production app, and `promote_app` to production fails its licence check ("is in staging (sandbox builds only)") until the product is in production. The runtime API serves only products in production (each one's frozen developer contract is made when it is published), so sandbox runtime calls on a staging product wait for production. Editing a staging product keeps it in staging; it needs `test_product` again before production.
4. `promote_product` to **production** publishes it, with exactly what publishing has always needed: the latest test passed **and** the product hasn't changed since, its v2 definition still checks out, a verified licence covers it (the firm's own, or a licence provider's sponsorship of every component it doesn't provide itself), and its underlying products are published. A production product's pending draft version (`create_product_version`) goes live the same way, while the product stays in production. `publish_product` still works as before, as a promotion to production, straight from an idea too (production's checks include staging's), with the same refusals.
5. `demote_product` from production to staging takes it out of the catalog as `unpublish_product` does (existing enrollments are kept, new ones are blocked, products built on it pause their sales) and keeps it open to sandbox builds; from staging to idea closes it to sandbox builds. `unpublish_product` still hides a product as before; it then counts as an idea.

Only staging is stored (`products.stage`, nullable, `staging` or nothing): a published product is in production and anything else is an idea. Adding the column left it empty on every existing row, so published products stayed in production, drafts and unpublished products became ideas, and no product's availability changed. Publishing clears it.

### Archiving a product

A product in idea or staging that is no longer wanted (a test product, say) is archived rather than deleted: nothing is ever deleted, and a product whose liquidity pool has treasury records couldn't be. `archive_product({ product_id, reason })` and `unarchive_product({ product_id, reason? })`, by its owner only (an admin, for Mynt's reference products), each in the audit trail as `product_archived` (with the stage and reason) or `product_unarchived` (with the stage it returned to).

- An archived product leaves `list_my_products` (and so the studio's sidebar and Products tab); `list_my_products({ include_archived: true })` lists it flagged `archived: true` with `archived_at`.
- It leaves every build: `list_buildable_products` (sandbox too) skips it, `create_app` and `update_app` refuse it ("archived by its firm"), and builds of apps that already pinned it leave it out. Archiving a staging product takes it out of sandbox builds.
- It can't be promoted, published or demoted while archived (`get_product_promotion_checks`, `promote_product`, `publish_product`, `demote_product` say to unarchive it first).
- A product in production is refused: move it back first (`demote_product` to staging), then archive it.
- Its stage is kept, so `unarchive_product` puts it back where it was: an idea stays an idea, a staging product reopens to sandbox builds.

Stored as `products.archived_at` (nullable; added empty on every existing row, so no product moved).

Bundled catalog products are read-only and pass the same checks.

## What a developer ships

```
my-app/
├── compose.yaml          api + web (+ mobile web export), hardened: read-only, no capabilities, no host network
├── .env.example          the app key and webhook secret, for api/ only
├── api/                  server: sessions, contracts, webhooks, server-side actions
├── web/                  web app: the journey runner, secure inputs, hosted flows
├── mobile/               Expo app (or Kotlin / Swift / Flutter), same journeys on a client session
├── solana/               optional: an Anchor program (smart contract) and its tests
└── packages/mynt-sdk/    the generated SDK
```

**Solana programs.** When an app needs a program on Solana, the agents write it next to the app and Mynt takes it from there: it rebuilds the program itself with Anchor's verifiable build in a clean sandbox, tests it on a local validator, deploys exactly those bytes, upgrades it from later verified builds, and sends the program's events to the firm's webhooks. Mynt signs on devnet; mainnet stays off until an admin configures its signer (a key in Mynt's vault, a key-custody service, or a multisig). Customers never see any of it: they see dollars. See [Solana programs](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference.md#solana-programs-developers).

Behind it is a whole coding team. An **architect** plans. **Server**, **web** and **mobile engineers** build their parts. A read-only **compliance reviewer** checks every product's contract and build terms. **QA** runs every journey against the sandbox. A **release engineer** ships the Compose project.

pages.title: Products & primitives
pages.markdown:
## A product is a composition

Nobody designs a financial product from scratch on Mynt. You compose one from regulated building blocks called **primitives**. Each primitive is a line of business (credit, payments, insurance, …) joined to an action on it (issuance, sale, servicing, …):

- a recurring deposit is a recurring payment mandate plus a term deposit;
- a foreign-currency transfer is a currency exchange plus a payment.

Because the product is made of primitives, its regulatory regime follows from them: which regulators supervise it, which licences may provide each part, and which obligations, filings and controls apply. Mynt works all of this out from its regulatory model, so nobody has to remember it, and then checks the product's legal entity, its parties and their GRC folders against the result.

Changing a product means re-composing it, not rebuilding it. Add a part, change who provides it or tighten a term, and the new definition is checked against the regime before it goes live.

## Product lines, actions and primitives

Product lines group products by **economic function**, not asset class: what a product does for the person or firm using it. Every product has one `product_line`:

- **credit**: lending and debt instruments, issued or bought: cards, personal/home/auto/education/gold loans, BNPL, working-capital loans, leasing, government and corporate bonds, T-bills, commercial paper
- **securitization**: pooling assets into securities: PTCs, ABS/MBS, direct assignment, co-lending pools, REIT/InvIT unit issuance, asset reconstruction
- **payments**: moving money: acceptance, payouts, mandates, wallets, remittances, CBDC
- **account_operations**: holding and running money: savings, current, term and recurring deposits, sweep accounts, money-market accounts, certificates of deposit, cash management
- **custody_settlement**: safekeeping and settlement: custody, depositories, clearing and CCPs, escrow, trustees, vaults
- **wealth**: investment exposure: mutual funds (money-market and liquid funds too), ETFs, equities, PMS/AIF, REIT/InvIT units bought as an investment, government savings schemes, and retirement products such as pensions, provident funds, 401(k)s and IRAs
- **insurance**: term/whole life, health, motor, home, travel, ULIPs, annuities
- **guarantees_trade**: bank guarantees, letters of credit, surety, credit and deposit guarantee schemes, factoring, supply-chain and export finance
- **exchange**: currency conversion, securities trading and execution, commodities and bullion trading, digital assets
- **derivatives**: forwards, swaps, futures, options
- **information**: credit bureaus, account aggregators, ratings, KYC registries, market data

A product that spans functions is a **composition** of primitives, not a line of its own. A cross-border transfer is an exchange primitive (the currency conversion) plus a payments primitive (moving the money). Retirement is wealth plus a statutory wrapper, and commodities are an underlying, not a line.

The **primitive is the line itself**. A product component is a line with an action, in a country. Collateral, customer segment and purpose aren't attributes of the primitive: they are the product's business context (collateral, for instance, is a source of value in underwriting). What a component falls under in a country, its **perimeter**, is every regulated product type there whose category is on that line and which allows the action. Who supervises it, which licences may provide it, and the law recorded against it all follow from that perimeter. Each regulated product type lists the **actions** that can be taken on it:

- **issuance**: creating it as the issuer
- **sale**: distributing it for its issuer
- **purchase**: buying it
- **secondary_sale**: selling it on after purchase
- **repackaging**: bundling it into something else
- **advice**: advising on it
- **servicing**: running it after the sale (collections, reconciliation, record-keeping)
- **underwriting**: taking on its risk or guaranteeing its placement
- **assessment**: producing an independent rating, valuation, index, actuarial certification, audit or accreditation of it

Two optional attributes describe the primitive itself:

- `underlying`: what it is made of: `cash`, `securities`, `commodities`, `real_assets`, `receivables`, `risk`, `data` or `digital_assets`
- `wrapper`: a statutory or tax structure around it: `statutory_pension`, `tax_advantaged` or `government_scheme`

### Product definitions (v2)

A product's full definition follows [`core/schemas/financial-product.v2.schema.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/financial-product.v2.schema.json).

**What it contains**
- **Components**, each a line × action, joined by typed composition links. The link types are:
  - `funds`, `settles_into`, `converts_into`, `repays_from`, `co_funds`;
  - `guarantees`, `secures`, `covers`, `wraps`;
  - `requires`, `excludes`, `feeds_data`, `services`;
  - `discovers_price_for`, which makes an exchange component a marketplace.
- **Business context around them:** customer segments, core algorithms, risk models, partner handoffs, terms, rates, fees, limits, servicing policies, lifecycle events and costs.
- **Connections:** every link between nodes is a typed connection with its own schema, and no node holds lists of other nodes' ids.
- **Upstream records by reference:** the register's personas and items, the owner's licences, roster parties and GRC records are connection targets, never copied in.

**How it's checked.** `check_product_definition` validates a definition, and `set_product_definition` validates it before saving. The checks:
- the JSON Schema;
- that every connection end resolves, including upstream records, which must be real and current;
- the composition rules:
  - the allowed primitive × action at each end of a link;
  - exactly one provider per component;
  - a partner handoff to every party that provides a component;
  - exactly one primary risk model per algorithm;
  - every risk model governed by a GRC record, owned by an internal party.

Every error comes back at once. A valid definition checked against a product (`product_id`) also lists `publish_blockers`: what its regime would refuse at publish, such as an uncovered component or a mandated stakeholder who isn't bound to the component it serves. Innovators and their agents read the schema itself over MCP as the resource `mynt://schemas/financial-product.v2`.

**What saving does**
- It sets the product's composition and parties, so the regime, the publish checks, pins and drift all keep working.
- It sets the catalogue record from the definition's projection, so existing tools, SDKs and apps keep reading the same fields.
- On a live product, it goes into the draft version.

**Handoffs to a vendor's standard service.** A `handoff_to_party` connection may name `attributes.vendor_subscription_id` (and, for readers, `service_type`): the firm's subscription to a vendor's offering. The party must be that subscription's vendor (subscribing adds it to the roster), `consent_purpose` the service type's, and the handoff's `sends.required` must include the service type's required inputs (so devices can collect them). The handoff's client action is then served by the vendor. Both attributes are optional; definitions without them are unchanged. See [Vendors](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference.md#vendors-standard-services-per-region).

**At publish.** The definition is checked again, since parties, licences and records may have changed. Its hash is then pinned as `pins.definition_hash`, and handoffs bound to vendor subscriptions as `pins.vendor_bindings`.

**Developer contract.** Publishing a defined product freezes its **developer contract**: exactly what developers build against. It comes from `get_developer_contract`, and it's also returned by `get_product_sdk`. Innovators preview it in `check_product_definition`.
- **Offers** per customer segment: eligibility, terms, rates, fees and customer-facing limits, with segment overrides applied.
- **Actions:**
  - `view_offers`;
  - each partner handoff, as the provider's hosted flow on the customer's device, with its consent purpose and typed inputs and outputs;
  - each customer-triggered lifecycle event, as an idempotent server call.
- **Lifecycle events** an app can listen to, the **consent purposes** it must hold and the **documents** it must show.
- **Never included:** algorithms, risk models, fraud and velocity controls, costs, revenue shares and the parties behind the product.

Each version's contract carries a `contract_hash`, which changes whenever the contract does.

**Product GRC folders.** Each product has its own GRC folder: `file_grc_record` and `get_grc_folder` with `product_id`. This is where, for example, the governance of the product's risk models lives.

**The reference catalogue's definitions.** Mynt's reference products have no firm, so their definitions name no providers, partner handoffs or risk models (those belong to the firm that offers the product, with its consent purposes and its model governance), but they carry everything else: components, segments, algorithms, terms, rates, fees, limits, servicing, lifecycle events and the register obligations each part satisfies. Admins save one with `set_product_definition`, then `test_product` and `publish_product` publish it as the product's next version, with a developer contract. [`core/schemas/examples/seed/`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/examples/seed/) holds definitions for `savings-account`, `fixed-deposit`, `recurring-deposit` and `personal-loan` (India), each with its sources and assumptions in `descriptions.long`. They point at the RBI in India's regulatory model: regulator `rbi` with the personas `rbi_resident_individual`, `rbi_senior_citizen` and `rbi_retail_borrower`, and the universal bank licence `rbi_universal_bank` with the thirteen `rbi_*` obligations they cite. [`core/schemas/regulatory/in.additions.json`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/schemas/regulatory/in.additions.json) adds exactly those to a server that already has the RBI and that licence, as production does, and only adds (see the regulatory model script below); apply it first. [`core/test/seed-regulatory-model.js`](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/core/test/seed-regulatory-model.js) builds a slice shaped like production's and applies it. The catalogue cites the regulator whose licence types grant the lead component's product type, preferring the one whose licence the definition's register items cite, so these four cite RBI. To apply them to a server:

```sh
# in the repository's core/ folder
node scripts/apply-seed-definitions.mjs --url <the server's MCP URL> --login --dry-run   # sign in in the browser, check only
node scripts/apply-seed-definitions.mjs --url <the server's MCP URL> --login             # check, save, test, publish
```

`--login` signs you in through your browser the way an MCP client does: OAuth discovery from the MCP URL, dynamic client registration, the authorization code flow with PKCE and a state check, the callback at `http://localhost:<port>/callback`, listening on the loopback addresses (`127.0.0.1` and `::1`) only. The access token stays in memory: it is never printed or saved. Instead of `--login`, an admin token can be set in the shell as `MYNT_ADMIN_TOKEN`; a token is never accepted on the command line.

The script checks every file first (`check_product_definition` with the product id) and changes nothing if any is invalid or has publish blockers, printing the errors and blockers. Otherwise it saves, tests and publishes each one and prints one line per product. A product whose live definition already matches is skipped. Pass file paths to apply only some.

## Versioning

A published product is never edited in place:
- `create_product_version` drafts the next version with a changelog. `test_product` and `publish_product` then act on that draft, with the same gates as a new product. The live version keeps serving until the draft is published.
- `list_product_versions` and `diff_product_versions` show the history.
- `restore_product_version` drafts a rollback as a new version, so history stays linear.
- Enrollments remember the version they joined on. `upgrade_enrollments` moves all of them to the live version, and a consumer can `upgrade_enrollment` their own.

## The product desk

The desk answers one question for a firm: does this product make sense, financially and legally? Each firm connects its own GitHub repository as its **workspace** (`connect_desk_repository`, after installing the Mynt GitHub App on it). Its computational logic accumulates there as models: `models/<name>/model.json` declares which products a model applies to, the inputs it needs, and how to run it. The code reads the product, its term sheet and the relevant regulation, and writes a report: a verdict (feasible, marginal or infeasible), metrics, checks that cite the law by `legal_ref`, and stress scenarios.

Work is split by what it needs:
- **Code runs (no AI).** `analyze_product` checks the workspace for a model that applies. If the product's term sheet (`set_product_terms`) has that model's inputs, Mynt clones the repository in a sandbox and executes the model. This is deterministic and re-runnable, costs cents, and never involves an agent. The clone token is removed before any model code runs. If inputs are missing, you get the list to fill in.
- **Agent tasks (intelligence).** If no model applies yet, or you ask for one with `desk_task` (e.g. "add an ALM liquidity ladder for our FD book"), the desk agent takes over. That's Claude Code in a sandbox, through Mynt's agent proxy. It designs the model, chooses and states the assumptions, interprets the regulation from the admins' model, and writes the code and tests on a branch. All arithmetic happens in code. **Mynt then runs that branch itself** in a clean sandbox with no credentials, saves that report, and opens a pull request on the workspace with Mynt's numbers. The agent's own numbers are never used.

`test_product` adds an advisory `feasibility` check from the latest report for the current term sheet, and reports stale when the terms changed. `get_product_terms` shows the term sheet and its analysis; `list_desk_jobs`, `get_desk_job` and `stop_desk_job` track the work.

**Configuration:** a sandbox provider key and the GitHub App, plus a model backend for agent tasks. Optional: `DESK_JOB_CAP_USD` (per agent task, default 5), `DESK_RUN_CAP_USD` (per code run, default 1) and `DESK_MONTHLY_CAP_USD` (per firm, default 50; unfinished jobs count at their cap).

**Algorithm explorations.** A product's decision algorithms (the eligibility, underwriting, limit, pricing and fraud-screening entries in its `core_algorithms`) can be improved by experiment. `start_exploration` names one algorithm, an objective to maximise (`net_margin`, `approved_volume`, …) and its constraints: a loss-rate ceiling, an APR cap, a minimum adverse-impact ratio (default 0.8), and reason codes on every decline.
- **Synthetic data.** Mynt generates applicants from the product, deterministically and from a seed (`core/src/explore-data.ts`). It makes a dev set with outcomes for the explorers, and a holdout only Mynt sees. Its assumptions are saved on the job.
- **The explorers.** Up to five run, each taking a different angle (`core/workspaces/algorithm-explorer/angles.json`). They loop in the autoresearch style: one change to the algorithm's folder, a short experiment with Mynt's scorer on the dev set, then keep the change or revert it, logged in `explore-log.tsv`. Each pushes every kept state to its own branch. Its push token is a file that Mynt refreshes, never an environment variable.
- **Mynt's ranking.** Mynt runs each branch's `decide`, and the pinned version as a baseline, on the holdout in clean sandboxes. It runs exactly the commits it pinned: the baseline when the job starts, and each branch's head when its explorer finishes. The holdout comes from a random secret per job that only Mynt holds, so it can't be rebuilt from the job's id or data. Mynt scores the decisions itself (`core/src/explore-score.ts`): the objective, the constraints, and stability over three time slices. Variants that fail a constraint rank below those that pass.
- **Adoption.** `adopt_variant` opens a pull request from a branch Mynt creates at the scored commit. An APR cap is required to start. The product changes only when you merge it and pin the new `version`.

`get_exploration` and `stop_exploration` track the work. Explorers share one cap (`EXPLORE_CAP_USD`, default 20) within the firm's monthly desk budget. `EXPLORE_MAX_ITERATIONS` and `EXPLORE_MAX_MINUTES` bound each explorer's loop.

pages.markdown:
## Who does what

- **Innovators are the licensed layer.** Any firm doing a regulated financial action:
  - issuing a product (a bank, NBFC, AMC or insurer)
  - selling another issuer's product (a mutual fund distributor, insurance broker, lending service provider)
  - repackaging others' products (a model portfolio)

  Each innovator acts for a **firm** (`create_entity`) and registers the **licences** it holds (`register_license`), which an admin verifies against the regulator's register (`review_license`). A product declares its `action` (`issuance`, `sale` or `repackaging`, with `underlying_product_ids` for the last two). **`publish_product` requires a verified, in-date licence held by the firm that covers that action on that category in that region.**
- **Developers are the software layer.** They build SDKs, apps and experiences on innovators' products, and never issue, sell, hold funds or collect financial data. Onboarding, KYC and payments hand off to the innovator's own flow (`deep_link` / `initiate_onboarding`).
- **Vendors offer standard services** that innovators plug into their products instead of each integrating them: identity checks, KYC records, account data, bank statement analytics, bureau reports, documents, e-sign, e-mandates. See [Vendors](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference.md#vendors-standard-services-per-region).
- **Liquidity providers** are firms or funds, added by an admin, that put capital into products' pools and take it out, watching each product's health to decide where capital goes. They get their own tools and none of a builder's or a consumer's; an admin isn't one. See [Liquidity pools](https://github.com/never2average/mynt/blob/main/docs/reference.md#liquidity-pools).

**Opening products to developers.** Each product has an **access mode**, set with `set_product_access`:

| Mode | Developers |
| --- | --- |
| `open` | Build and publish any experience that meets the terms |
| `approval` (default) | Build now; go live once the innovator approves their request |
| `private` | Only developers the innovator invites (`invite_developer`) |

Each product also has **build terms**:
- **permitted actions:** display, compare, prefill, deep_link, embed_widget, initiate_onboarding
- **required disclosures**
- **banned phrases**
- **allowed customer personas**
- **branding**
- **commercials:** none, referral fee or revenue share
- **handoff_url:** where runtime API hand-offs send the user (https)

**On the developer side:**
- **Find products:** `list_buildable_products` and `get_product_sdk` (data shape, sandbox sample, permitted actions, hand-offs).
- **Ask for access:** `request_product_access` and `list_my_requests`.
- **Check and publish:** `check_experience`, then `publish_app`. Publishing needs access to every product **and** a passing check against each product's terms.

**On the innovator side:**
- **Inbox:** `list_requests` and `review_request` (approve or reject, with a note).
- **Visibility:** `list_experiences` shows every app using their products.
- **Control:** `revoke_access`, and **`suspend_product_experiences`** as a kill switch (the product goes private, every grant is revoked, and live campaigns using it are paused).

**Campaigns.** Promoting a financial product is a regulated act, and Mynt treats it as one:
- A campaign over the launcher's own (or their firm's) products, or the open reference catalogue, goes live once its copy passes the lint.
- A campaign over **another innovator's** products becomes `pending_approval` and lands in that innovator's inbox. It goes live when every product's innovator approves, and drops back to draft on any rejection.

## SDKs and experiences

**SDKs.** `create_sdk(name, languages, product_ids)` defines an SDK over products you can build on: open or approval products, or private ones you were invited to. `generate_sdk_release(sdk_id, version, changelog)` then writes an immutable, semver-versioned bundle:
- `openapi.json`: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the app API (`GET /v1/products`, `GET /v1/products/{id}`, `POST /v1/handoffs`, `POST /v1/events`, signed webhooks), with a schema per product built from its fields.
- `typescript/`: `src/schema.d.ts` generated from the document by [openapi-typescript](https://openapi-ts.dev), an [openapi-fetch](https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-fetch/) client for every operation, and a thin `core/src/index.ts` of Mynt helpers: `createMyntClient`, `startHandoff` (typed to each product's permitted hand-offs), `trackEvent`, `verifyWebhook`, and constants for every product's required disclosures, branding and banned phrases (`disclosuresFor(id)`).
- `python/`: `generate.sh` runs [openapi-python-client](https://github.com/openapi-generators/openapi-python-client) on the document to produce the client, plus a standard-library `mynt_helpers.py` (`verify_webhook`, `disclosures_for`, `check_handoff`, the same constants). openapi-python-client is not a Mynt dependency; tests use it only when installed (set `OPENAPI_PYTHON_CLIENT` to its path to point at a virtualenv).

`list_sdks`, `list_sdk_releases` and `get_sdk_release` (files as `{path, content}`) flag a release **stale**, with reasons, when a product has published a newer version, changed its build terms, been unpublished, or your access was revoked. Generate a new release to pick the changes up. `get_product_sdk` still describes a single product.

**Experiences.** `set_experience(app_id, experience)` gives an app a structured definition: screens of `product_card`, `comparison_table`, `calculator` (maturity, emi, sip), `disclosure_block`, `handoff_cta` and `text` components. On top of the terms lint, `check_experience` and `publish_app` then require:
- every screen showing a product also carries that product's `disclosure_block`, which renders its required disclosures verbatim
- CTAs use only hand-offs the product permits, and comparisons only products that permit `compare`
- components reference only the app's products
- no banned phrase in any title, text or label

`render_experience_preview(app_id)` returns a self-contained HTML page (no scripts or external assets, everything escaped) with product data, disclosures and branding, for review.

## Campaigns

- **Segments** pick consumers by what they currently hold: `enrolled_in`, `enrolled_in_lines`, and `not_enrolled_in` for cross-sell.
- **Campaigns** target a segment (or everyone) on chosen channels, with up to 5 copy variants for A/B tests.
- **`lint_campaign`** checks every variant against its products. It blocks guaranteed or risk-free claims for products that can lose value, requires a market-risk disclosure for market-linked products, and requires interest/fee disclosure for credit. `launch_campaign` refuses copy that fails.
- **Attribution.** Live campaigns show up in consumers' `list_offers`. Each consumer always sees the same variant, and `enroll_in_product` with the offer's `campaign_id` is attributed. `get_campaign_metrics` reports audience, enrollments, conversion, and results per variant and per product.
